result.summary: Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md, docs/Design system for AI agents/readme.md, docs/agents/anti-patterns.md, docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md (full), docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md (full), decisions/0004-telegram-framework-grammy.md, and every changed file in git diff master...HEAD. Resolved both flagged deviations, confirmed the derive-then-gate discipline live, ran lint/build/vitest independently, and found a live-reproducible functional regression BACKEND-DEV's own handoff explicitly flagged as untested -- that regression is the reason for this FAIL. No design-system findings apply (bot surface has no UI component, confirmed against REQ-019.md §9). DEVIATION 1 (Context import in domain/onboarding.ts) -- RESOLVED, not blocking. Read REQ-019.md §3.2 myself: it states `advanceOnboarding(ctx: Context, ...)` explicitly and reasons it mirrors handlers/start.ts's own pre-existing assignChapterOrPrompt convention (decide-and-reply in one function). This is a genuine design specification, not something BACKEND-DEV introduced unilaterally, and that design passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR twice (handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-01b-design-validator-regate.json) with this exact text present both times. Per core-directives.md's instruction-precedence rule, a decisions/ record is never silently overridden in either direction -- I am not resolving this as a contradiction, I am flagging it forward: decisions/0004's own consequence text ('domain logic ... goes in framework-free modules that handlers call, never inside handler bodies') does not carve out an exception for a thin decide-and-send composition function, yet this codebase now has two of them (assignChapterOrPrompt in handlers/start.ts, and now advanceOnboarding in domain/onboarding.ts -- the second one explicitly placed in a domain/ file). The substantive property decision 0004 protects (business rules stay unit-testable without grammY) IS preserved here: the actual rule, determineOnboardingStep, is pure and covered by onboarding.test.ts with zero grammY import; advanceOnboarding is a thin dispatcher on top of it, the same shape as the already-reviewed precedent. I am not blocking on this, but filing it forward as a MINOR finding for ORCH to route to a decisions/0004 addendum clarifying that a pure-decision-plus-thin-dispatch split satisfies the framework-free intent even when the dispatcher itself is named/located in domain/ and imports Context -- so a future reviewer does not have to re-litigate this from scratch. DEVIATION 2a (advanceOnboarding's 'chapter-needed' third return value) -- RESOLVED, not blocking on its own. REQ-019.md §3.2 step 4's own prose already requires a caller-visible 'chapter-needed' outcome ("the caller runs assignChapterOrPrompt itself ... advanceOnboarding is called again") -- the design's literal `Promise<"prompted" | "ready">` type annotation just under-specifies its own step 4. Widening the return type to include "chapter-needed" is implementing the design's own stated behavior correctly, not inventing new behavior. Legitimate and necessary for handlers/profile.ts's entry points, which (unlike /start's three call sites) have no pre-existing chapter gate. Not a CODE-DESIGNER rework item -- filed forward as a MINOR doc-accuracy note only. DEVIATION 2b / THE BLOCKER -- BACKEND-DEV's own issue #2 flagged that the zero-active-chapters interim choice was 'not exercised by any of REQ-019's own 6 ACs ... no live evidence was captured for this specific path.' Per this run's task instruction to re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about (core-directives.md), I constructed that exact condition myself against a fresh scratch Postgres with ZERO chapters seeded (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml) and reproduced a genuine functional regression: Sequence: /start (tg_id 1000000902) -> consent:agree callback. assignChapterOrPrompt correctly detects zero active chapters, sends `start.noActiveChapters` ('Отделения пока недоступны.'), and returns "continue" -- users.chapter_id stays NULL, exactly REQ-014's own already-established behavior for this branch. makeConsentCallbackHandler then calls `advanceOnboarding(ctx, db, flowUser.id, true, (finalUser?.chapterId ?? flowUser.chapterId) !== null, finalLang)` -- hasChapter evaluates to FALSE (chapterId is still null), so determineOnboardingStep correctly returns {kind:"chapter-needed"}, and advanceOnboarding returns the literal string "chapter-needed" per its own code (domain/onboarding.ts line 84-86: `if (step.kind === "chapter-needed") { return "chapter-needed"; }` -- no reply sent). Back in makeConsentCallbackHandler: `if (outcome !== "ready") { return; // "prompted" already sent the next question }` -- outcome is "chapter-needed", not "prompted" or "ready", so this returns silently. NO reply is ever sent after the noActiveChapters message. Confirmed by inspecting the full `captured` array from a live bot.handleUpdate() dispatch: exactly 3 entries (consent prompt, answerCallbackQuery, noActiveChapters text) then nothing -- no greeting, no profile prompt, no error. I diffed this against the pre-REQ-019 code myself (`git show d7458ae~1:apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts`): the old makeStartHandler unconditionally called `await ctx.reply(getCatalog(finalLang).start.greeting);` immediately after the chapter-assignment block, regardless of whether chapterId ended up null (0 active chapters) or set. This is a REAL, confirmed behavioral regression against REQ-019.md §3.3's own explicit written guarantee: "No behavioral change for any user whose profile is already complete or who has not yet reached the profile stage in a way this requirement's own acceptance criteria exercise -- the greeting is byte-for-byte the same reply it always was in that case." A zero-active-chapters user is exactly a user who "has not yet reached the profile stage" in a way no AC exercises, and their behavior changed: they now get silently stuck forever (chapterId can never become non-null through this path, so every subsequent /start repeats the identical dead end) instead of receiving the greeting. This affects all THREE of start.ts's modified call sites (makeStartHandler, makeChapterCallbackHandler is unaffected since it only fires once a chapter WAS assigned, but makeConsentCallbackHandler and makeStartHandler's own direct chapterId===null path both hit it) whenever a chapter/deployment genuinely has zero active chapters -- a real, already-supported REQ-014 state (the `noActiveChapters` catalog key exists specifically for it), not a contrived scenario. This is BACKEND-DEV's own domain/handlers to fix, not a CODE-DESIGNER rework: the design's §3.3 guarantee is correct and does not need to change; the implementation at handlers/start.ts's two affected call sites needs to handle a "chapter-needed" outcome from advanceOnboarding the same way handlers/profile.ts's own `reachReadyOrPrompt` helper already does (loop/retry or fall through to the greeting), rather than silently returning. Concretely: makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler both need the equivalent of profile.ts's chapter-needed handling before treating a non-"ready" outcome as "already replied, nothing to do." OTHER CHECKS PERFORMED, ALL CLEAN: - Derive-then-gate discipline (REQ-019.md §4.6): read all three callback handlers (makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler, makeProfileStudentCallbackHandler, makeProfileExperienceCallbackHandler) plus the text/contact listeners in apps/bot/src/handlers/profile.ts -- every one derives `step` fresh from a DB read gated by `hasConsented && hasChapter` BEFORE any write function is named, and gates the write on `step.kind === "profile-field" && step.field === `, exactly as designed. Independently live-verified with a forged `profile:skip:phone` callback AND a forged free-text answer dispatched against a user with consent_pd_at still NULL (fresh scratch Postgres, tg_id 1000000901): profiles row count = 0 before and after, users.consent_pd_at still NULL after, the callback was answered and the identical consent prompt was re-shown, no exception. This is the exact attack the design gate previously FAILed on, reproduced live against the actual merged code, not trusted from BACKEND-DEV's report. - Migration (apps/bot/drizzle/0004_fancy_zombie.sql): matches REQ-019-schema.md §5's predicted 11 statements exactly (6 DROP NOT NULL, 5 ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT false), applied cleanly via `drizzle-kit migrate` against a fresh Postgres 16 container. schema.ts matches the migration and the schema doc's column table 1:1. Not a drop/rewrite of PII content (S13 sign-off correctly not required, per REQ-019-schema.md §6's own reasoning, which I independently agree with -- DROP NOT NULL widens legality, rewrites no existing row). - S11: grepped apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts, domain/onboarding.ts, handlers/profile.ts for any log.*/writeAuditLog call myself -- zero matches in all three files (confirmed independently, not copied from BACKEND-DEV's grep). log.ts's REDACTED_KEYS set (phone, email, plus config secrets) is unchanged and genuinely wired through every write() call -- no bypass. - npm run lint: 0 errors (2 pre-existing apps/web warnings, unrelated). npm run build: tsc clean for apps/bot. npx vitest run: 24 files / 284 tests passed (exceeds the 142+ BACKEND-DEV reported at merge time, which itself exceeded the 142-test floor named in this run's task). - No design-system/token/copy findings: bot surface has no CSS/visual component (REQ-019.md §9), all new strings are plain catalog keys following the existing profile.*/venue.*/event.* convention; catalogs.test.ts's runtime parity check still enforces ru.ts/en.ts/types.ts lock-step. Scratch verification scripts (apps/bot/scratch-verify-reviewer.ts, apps/bot/scratch-verify-ac1.ts) were written, run, then deleted; `docker compose down -v` torn down the scratch Postgres; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean before writing this handoff.

issues.description: handlers/start.ts's makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler do not handle a "chapter-needed" outcome from advanceOnboarding. In a deployment/chapter-state with zero active chapters (REQ-014's own already-supported noActiveChapters branch), assignChapterOrPrompt returns "continue" but leaves users.chapter_id permanently NULL; the subsequent advanceOnboarding call then always returns "chapter-needed" (never "prompted" or "ready"), and both call sites' `if (outcome !== "ready") return;` treats this as "already replied" when nothing was sent. Live-reproduced: after /start + consent:agree with zero chapters seeded, the user receives the noActiveChapters message and then silently nothing -- no greeting, no profile prompt, forever (chapterId can never resolve). This regresses pre-REQ-019 behavior (confirmed by diffing against d7458ae~1: the old code unconditionally sent start.greeting after the chapter block) and violates REQ-019.md §3.3's own explicit written guarantee of no behavioral change for a user who has not reached the profile stage in an AC-exercised way. Fix: give makeStartHandler and makeConsentCallbackHandler the same "chapter-needed" handling handlers/profile.ts's reachReadyOrPrompt helper already has (retry/fall through), or an equivalent that still reaches the greeting when chapter assignment resolves to "continue" with no chapter ever assigned. Route to BACKEND-DEV.

decisions/0004-telegram-framework-grammy.md's consequence text ('domain logic ... goes in framework-free modules ... never inside handler bodies') has no stated exception for a thin decide-and-send composition function, yet this codebase now has two (handlers/start.ts's assignChapterOrPrompt, and domain/onboarding.ts's advanceOnboarding -- the latter explicitly in a domain/ file and importing Context). REQ-019.md §3.2 deliberately specifies this shape and passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR twice; the substantive property decision 0004 protects (the actual business rule stays framework-free and unit-testable) is preserved via determineOnboardingStep being pure and separately tested. Not blocking this gate. Recommend ORCH route a decisions/0004 addendum clarifying that a pure-decision-plus-thin-dispatch split satisfies the framework-free intent, so a future reviewer/BACKEND-DEV does not re-litigate this from a cold start.

REQ-019.md §3.2's advanceOnboarding signature is documented as returning Promise<"prompted" | "ready">, but the same section's own step 4 prose requires a third, caller-visible "chapter-needed" outcome. The implementation's 3-value return type is correct and necessary (confirmed against the design's own prose); only the design doc's type annotation is stale. Recommend a follow-up correction note on REQ-019.md itself (same convention as REQ-014.md's/REQ-016.md's own correction-note precedent), not a rework.
